title: Hermes Helm Chart Values
description: JSON Schema for validating Hermes Helm chart values at install time
$comment: additionalProperties:false is applied to the Hermes-owned objects only. The postgresql/redis/nats/centrifugo keys are forwarded wholesale to sub-charts that have their own schemas, so constraining them here would reject every legitimate sub-chart override — including the per-image `registry` pins values.yaml sets to stop the NATS chart inheriting global.image.registry. Top-level additionalProperties is false so a misspelled section (services:, networkPolicies:, replicaCount:, cleanup:, a top-level image:) is rejected at install time instead of silently falling back to chart defaults. That means every key values.yaml sets must appear below; scripts/check_helm_render.py is what keeps the two in step, because it renders the chart rather than reading the schema.

rateLimit.$comment: Only the four HTTP services (send, admin, inbox, user) read these; it lives on the shared service definition rather than in four copies. burst/perSecond accept "" to mean 'keep the service default', which is why they are not plain integers.

concurrency.$comment: Dispatch only, on the shared service definition for the same reason rateLimit is: the alternative is a near-duplicate of this whole block, and a copy drifts. Setting it on another service renders nothing.
concurrency.description: Dispatch worker pool size (HERMES_DISPATCH_CONCURRENCY). The chart's largest throughput lever -- 8 workers reach 2,100 msg/s where 64 reach 7,907 (cmd/dispatchbench, Longhorn-backed Postgres). Costs one Postgres connection per worker; database.maxConns follows it automatically.

database.$comment: Dispatch only, as with concurrency above. HERMES_DATABASE_MAX_CONNS is read by every service, but the chart renders it for dispatch alone -- putting it in the shared ConfigMap would size all nine pools from a number tuned for one.

maxConns.description: Postgres pool for dispatch (HERMES_DATABASE_MAX_CONNS). Empty derives concurrency + 2, which is the intended usage: cmd/dispatch clamps its worker pool to this value, so a pool set below concurrency silently discards the extra workers. The chart refuses that combination rather than clamping it.

podDisruptionBudget.$comment: maxUnavailable only, no minAvailable. minAvailable at or above the replica count pins disruptionsAllowed to zero permanently and blocks every node drain, which is why the production overlay moved off it; not offering the option is cheaper than documenting the footgun.

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: Overrides hermes.shutdown.terminationGracePeriodSeconds for this service. It must cover the whole shutdown sequence — preStop sleep, in-process drain delay, NATS drain, HTTP shutdown — or the kubelet SIGKILLs the process partway through. scripts/check_shutdown_budget.py enforces the arithmetic over the rendered manifests.

global.$comment: Deliberately NOT closed. Helm merges `global` into every sub-chart, so this object legitimately carries keys this chart never reads — global.imageRegistry, global.storageClass and global.security.allowInsecureImages for the Bitnami charts, global.image.pullSecretNames for the NATS chart. Closing it rejects all of them, which was found the direct way: an install overriding global.security.allowInsecureImages was refused by the schema.

image.$comment: Also not closed: the NATS sub-chart reads global.image.pullPolicy and global.image.pullSecretNames from this same object.

registry.description: Registry for Hermes' own images. Note that Helm merges `global` into every sub-chart and the NATS chart reads this same key, which is why values.yaml pins nats.*.image.registry explicitly.

pullPolicy.description: Pull policy for every Hermes image, overridable per service. The NATS sub-chart reads this same key, so setting it here also applies to the bundled bus — which is consistent rather than surprising.

imagePullSecrets.description: Names of existing image pull secrets, applied to every Hermes pod. The chart does not create them.

env.description: Deployment environment, published as HERMES_ENV. internal/config/config.go treats ONLY the literal "development" as relaxed, so any other value — including a typo like "prod" or "staging" — takes the strict path in Config.Validate() and every workload exits unless all three datastores use TLS and all three secrets are real. The enum exists to turn such a typo into a clear install-time rejection rather than nine pods in CrashLoopBackOff with a validation error in their logs. If you genuinely need a third environment name, widen this enum and remember it will behave exactly like "production".

logLevel.$comment: Empty means 'keep the built-in default' — Debug in development, Info elsewhere — so the chart does not hardcode one. The enum catches a typo here rather than letting it fall through: bootstrap.logLevel() deliberately ignores an unrecognised value rather than exiting, so a mistyped level would silently leave the default in place with nothing to indicate it.
logLevel.description: Log level for every Hermes service (HERMES_LOG_LEVEL). Empty keeps the default, which is debug when hermes.env is development and info otherwise. Worth setting to info on any bundled install taking real traffic: per-request records live at debug, and a bundled install cannot leave development because Config.Validate() demands TLS on all three datastores outside it.

preStopSleepSeconds.description: Renders a preStop SleepAction, which needs Kubernetes 1.30+ (beta in 1.29) — hence the default of 0. Belt and braces only: the images are FROM scratch, so a preStop exec hook has no shell to run sleep in, and the drain delay that actually runs is in-process via HERMES_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_DELAY.

provider.description: Email delivery provider. Only smtp and ses are implemented: templates/configmap.yaml branches on exactly these two, and internal/email/email.go rejects anything else at startup. 'sendgrid' was previously accepted here, which passed helm install and then crash-looped the worker with 'unknown email provider'.

retentionDays.description: Number of days to retain notification events

streamReplicas.$comment: Empty derives it from the bundled cluster size. The built-in default of 1 meant a three-node bundled bus carried single-replica streams, so losing one node stopped the pipeline on a cluster sized to survive exactly that.

streamReplicasAllowChange.$comment: Permits altering the replication factor of streams that already exist, which migrates them between peers. Needed once when raising an existing installation's replica count; leaving it on makes every future replica change something a routine upgrade can trigger.

bootstrap.description: First API key, created at install time. Without it a fresh install cannot be authenticated against at all.

apiServerPort.description: Kubernetes API server port for the networkPolicy egress rule. 443 on managed control planes, 6443 on k3s/kind/k3d/RKE.

prober.$comment: Synthetic end-to-end prober. Not a $ref to #/definitions/service: it has no replicas (one, structurally -- N replicas multiply the write rate and turn the metric into an average over pods), no autoscaling, and no PDB, and it carries settings no other service has.

organizationID.$comment: UUID, not free text: organizations.id is UUID PRIMARY KEY, so a readable name cannot be inserted. The chart shipped 'hermes-synthetic' here, which made prober.enabled=true crash-loop on a 500 from /v1/auth/token.

centrifugoURL.$comment: The websocket CONNECTION endpoint (external port, /connection/websocket), not the HTTP API on the internal port. Pointing it at the API yields a socket that never connects and 100% reported loss against a healthy pipeline.

enabled.description: Run the JetStream stream provisioning Job (ADR 0005 phase 4). Send, dispatch and all four workers verify their streams at boot via messaging.EnsureStreams, which cannot create them, and exit non-zero if one is missing. Setting this to false without provisioning streams out of band leaves six deployments in CrashLoopBackOff.

rateLimit.$comment: Deployment-wide rate limiting. The per-credential rate is per service, under each service's own rateLimit block; these settings describe the installation.

perIP.$comment: Applied inside the Go services before authentication, so it works with any ingress controller or none. burst/perSecond accept "" to mean 'keep the service default'.

trustedProxyCIDRs.$comment: Empty means trust no forwarding headers at all. Never set this to 0.0.0.0/0: X-Forwarded-For is caller-supplied, so trusting every peer lets any caller pick its own bucket.

maxEntries.$comment: Per-credential buckets held per replica; "" keeps the built-in 50,000. Size against distinct callers active in a 30-minute window, which for inbox and user is the active user base rather than any request rate. Callers past the cap are admitted unlimited rather than refused (ADR 0024).

distributed.$comment: Runs the per-credential admission check in Redis so the configured rate is the cluster-wide ceiling. Requires Redis; degrades to per-replica enforcement if it is unavailable.

controller.description: Controller dialect to emit. Empty infers from className. nginx and Traefik express the realtime prefix strip differently and are not interchangeable.

rateLimit.$comment: Applied to the API ingress only; the realtime ingress is deliberately excluded because its connections are long-lived WebSockets.

endpoint.description: OTLP endpoint for the OpenTelemetry Collector

protocol.description: OTLP protocol used by Hermes services

force.$comment: Bypasses the .Capabilities.APIVersions check in templates/servicemonitor.yaml. That check keeps an evaluation install on a cluster without the Prometheus Operator from failing on an unknown kind, but it needs cluster access -- plain `helm template` and some GitOps renderers report no capabilities and drop every ServiceMonitor silently. Set true where the chart renders without a cluster and the CRDs are known present.
force.description: Render ServiceMonitors even when the renderer cannot see the monitoring.coreos.com/v1 CRD.

profiling.$comment: net/http/pprof on a dedicated port for every service, via HERMES_DEBUG_PORT in the shared ConfigMap. Off by default: the endpoint is unauthenticated and exposes the process command line and every goroutine stack, and the block/mutex profiles perturb what they measure. internal/bootstrap.StartDebugServer starts nothing when the port is 0.

blockProfileRate.description: Sample one blocking event per this many nanoseconds spent blocked. 0 disables; 1 records everything and is expensive.

mutexProfileFraction.description: Sample 1 in N mutex contention events. 0 disables.

image.description: Image for the `helm test` connectivity pod. Pinned, and settable so it can point at a mirror on an air-gapped cluster.

tls.$comment: TLS for the bundled datastores, which is what makes hermes.env=production possible with them. Requires cert-manager unless every enabled store carries a per-store tls.existingSecret.

create.$comment: Creates a namespaced CA. The private key then lives in this namespace, where any Secret reader can mint a certificate every Hermes service trusts -- deploy/k8s/pki/ moved that key out of the application namespace deliberately.

postgresql.$comment: Bundled evaluation Postgres, rendered by templates/postgresql.yaml. Closed, unlike the bitnami sub-chart block it replaced (ADR 0009): there is no longer a downstream schema to forward unknown keys to, so an unrecognised key here is a silent no-op rather than someone else's validation error. auth.* is required because hermes.databaseUrl builds HERMES_DATABASE_URL from it.

sslmode.$comment: disable, allow and prefer are absent on purpose: config.Validate() rejects all three, and allow/prefer specifically because libpq falls back to plaintext without saying so. require is permitted but is encryption without server authentication -- pgx sets InsecureSkipVerify for it.

maxConnections.$comment: Accepts "" to mean 'keep the postgres image default of 100', which is why it is not a plain integer -- the same convention rateLimit.burst uses. Exists because 100 does not stretch: nine services at the built-in pgx pool of 10 already claim 90, so tuning dispatch.concurrency past the default needs room made for it. templates/_validate.tpl refuses the install when the fleet's worst case exceeds this less a small reserve.
maxConnections.description: max_connections for the bundled Postgres. Empty keeps the image default of 100. Raise postgresql.resources alongside it.

extraSettings.$comment: Passed through verbatim as `-c key=value` server arguments by templates/postgresql.yaml, joining the ssl and max_connections settings collected there. Deliberately unvalidated: the point is to reach settings the chart does not model, and enumerating them would defeat that. Defaults to track_wal_io_timing=on, without which the postgres-exporter WAL query publishes a mean fsync latency of 0/0 -- a metric that always reads zero is worse than an absent one.
extraSettings.description: Extra `-c key=value` settings for the bundled Postgres, e.g. commit_delay=250 or shared_buffers=1GB.

shmSize.$comment: Size of the /dev/shm emptyDir. Kubernetes defaults a container to 64Mi regardless of node memory, and Postgres allocates parallel workers' shared memory there, so a parallel plan over a large table fails with 'could not resize shared memory segment'.

redis.$comment: Bundled evaluation Redis, rendered by templates/redis.yaml. No auth block, deliberately: HERMES_REDIS_URL is a ConfigMap value, so a password set here would be written beside it in plaintext. Use externalRedis for an authenticated instance. tls encrypts the connection but adds no authentication -- it raises the bar from anything on the network to any pod in this namespace.

metrics.$comment: redis_exporter sidecar. Redis serves no HTTP of its own, so without this there is no scrape target at all -- and this Redis holds the idempotency keys and, when Centrifugo runs the Redis engine, every realtime publication.

nats.$comment: Forwarded to the nats sub-chart. Deliberately not closed.

centrifugo.$comment: Forwarded to the centrifugo sub-chart. Deliberately not closed.
